name: Uptown
tagline: Mid-rise apartments, patios and the McKinney Avenue trolley
description: Dallas at its most walkable, a grid of new mid-rise apartment buildings, patio restaurants and gyms along McKinney Avenue, with the Katy Trail running along its western edge. Young professionals fill it. You can live here without driving daily, which is rare in this city.
bestFor: Remote workers who want to skip a car and have restaurants, gyms and coworking on foot.
pros: Genuinely walkable, plus the free M-Line trolley
Katy Trail for running and cycling
Newest apartment stock with fibre and gyms
cons: Highest rents in the city outside Highland Park
Bar noise on McKinney at weekends
Parking is scarce and usually paid

name: Deep Ellum
tagline: Murals, music venues and converted warehouses
description: The old warehouse district east of downtown, covered wall to wall in murals and packed with live music venues, tattoo studios, breweries and coffee roasters. Lofts sit above the bars. It is the creative heart of Dallas and the most characterful place to base yourself if you like noise and art.
bestFor: Creatives and night owls who want music, murals and loft living over suburban calm.
pros: Best live music and bar scene in Dallas
Walk or take the streetcar into downtown
cons: Loud until 2am on Elm and Main streets
Street crime and fights do happen late at night
Limited groceries, you drive for a proper supermarket

name: Bishop Arts District
tagline: Bungalow blocks and indie shops in North Oak Cliff
description: A compact walkable pocket in North Oak Cliff, just across the Trinity from downtown, where a few blocks of independent boutiques, bakeries and patio restaurants sit surrounded by 1920s bungalows. The crowd is a mix of long-time Latino families and newer arrivals, and rents undercut Uptown.
bestFor: Nomads who want neighbourhood character and better value than the north side of the river.
pros: Cheaper than Uptown for comparable walkability
Skyline views and quick drive into downtown
cons: The walkable core is only a few blocks wide
Transit into downtown is slow, most people drive

name: Lower Greenville
tagline: A restaurant strip fringed by quiet old-house streets
description: Greenville Avenue between Ross and Mockingbird is a solid run of restaurants, patios and neighbourhood bars, with tidy streets of 1920s frame houses and duplexes immediately behind it. The mix of nightlife on one street and quiet residential blocks a minute away suits people who want both.
bestFor: People who want a walkable bar and restaurant strip without living inside the noise.
pros: Excellent food and bar strip you can walk to
Quiet leafy residential streets one block back
Duplexes and houses instead of only apartment towers
cons: Weekend crowds and noise near the avenue
You still need a car for most errands
Older houses mean weaker insulation and higher summer bills

name: Downtown and the Arts District
tagline: High-rise loft living beside museums and Klyde Warren Park
description: Converted office towers and new high-rises in the central grid, next to the Dallas Museum of Art, the Winspear Opera House and Klyde Warren Park. Deals on large loft units are common because supply is high. Everything is close, but the streets can feel empty outside office hours.
bestFor: Short-stay nomads who want a big loft, transit access and museums within walking distance.
pros: Large converted lofts at good value per square foot
DART rail hub, easy airport access
Museums, park and arena all walkable
cons: Quiet and hollow on evenings and Sundays
Few grocery options for a district this dense
